options.configuration: Downstream OIDC login; one generic OIDC Enterprise Connection with inbound SCIM; no outbound bridge or paid add-ons

conditions: Register the consuming application and configure its callback URLs, allowed grants and intended client authentication; no tenant or application was tested.
This is downstream Auth0-to-application login, distinct from the upstream enterprise OIDC connection recorded under ENTERPRISE_SSO.
The recorded offer is B2B Free, not a trial, paid B2C tier or custom agreement; documentation does not guarantee future zero cost.

evidence.summary: Auth0 documents OIDC application configuration through tenant discovery metadata. This proposes configurable downstream login, not a verified deployment or authentication-control policy.

conditions: Use the single included Enterprise Connection from https://auth0.com/pricing; the B2B Free announcement at https://auth0.com/blog/auth0-b2b-plans-upgraded/ identifies this offer explicitly. Account entitlement and usage limits still require verification.
Register Auth0 with the upstream OIDC provider, configure issuer/client settings and enable that connection for the consuming application.
This option records one generic OIDC connection, not unlimited generic enterprise federation or a tested Okta/Entra ID integration.

evidence.summary: The enterprise OIDC guide describes upstream registration, connection setup and application enablement. The Free offer is a bounded documentation scope, not proof of multi-customer compatibility.

conditions: The public Free offer includes inbound SCIM at https://auth0.com/pricing; enable it on the supported generic OIDC Enterprise Connection with its own endpoint, operation-scoped token and attribute mapping.

For this OIDC path, match the upstream ID token sub to SCIM externalId as described at https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/protocols/scim/configure-inbound-scim-for-identity-providers-using-saml-or-openid.

This is inbound user lifecycle in Auth0, not native outbound SCIM to the SaaS. Do not infer app-local session revocation, back-channel logout entitlement or paid authorization features from this assertion.

evidence.summary: The guide documents connection-scoped inbound User CRUD and deactivation. Combined with the public Free inclusion, this proposes configurable SCIM, not tested application-side lifecycle enforcement.

conditions: Group endpoints are documented, but the inspected Free pricing offer does not distinguish group-specific entitlement; verify access and limits for this exact tenant before asserting scoped availability.
The native group schema accepts user members, not nested groups; group names must be unique within a connection.

Organization membership, role assignment and outbound event/application synchronization are separate configurations or entitlements, not consequences of an inbound group record. No outbound bridge is included here.
UNKNOWN must not be read as unsupported or silently promoted from the documented SCIM User availability.

evidence.summary: The guide describes Group operations with user-only membership and separate authorization/external-system integrations. It does not establish group access on this untested Free tenant.
